verdicts.reason: Verified. buildReadinessExport() writes `verdict`, `verdictLabel`, `totalScore`, `nextVerdict` and each area's `id`, `label`, `score` (readiness-export.ts:60-79). The next state appears only as its key (for example `inheritable_with_guardrails`), which is one of the names the owner replaced, and the scores have no scale in the file. The file's own header says it is meant to be opened by the founder and shared with advisors (readiness-export.ts:13-17). Severity 1 is right. The code paths are as described (read, not run against a database). bootReadinessHistory() takes the previous state only from this browser's saved copy (readiness-history.ts:72-92, 189); with no saved copy `previous` is null, `transition` is null, and a row with no change is still inserted (readiness-history.ts:210-234). The announcement reads only the newest row and stops when it has no change (ceremony.ts:99-106), its 'already shown' marker is per browser (ceremony.ts:27), and a failed write is dropped after the saved copy has been advanced (readiness-history.ts:158-166, 220-223). These are weaknesses that were there before the language work, not regressions from it, and medium confidence is right. The two code changes proposed would each make something worse. (a) Using the newest cloud row as the previous state on a browser with no saved copy: readiness is calculated from that browser's own stored copies of each area's data (readiness-aggregator.ts:6-16; the Dashboard page loads nothing from the cloud before calculating, src/dashboard/index.html:19-20), so a new browser usually calculates a lower state first. The change would record a false downward change and then false upward ones as the areas are opened, including a second arrival at 'Usable with founder support'. (b) Searching the last 50 rows for a qualifying change: with the marker kept per browser, every browser without it would then show the announcement, including a new seller's, which the code documents as not intended (ceremony.ts:21-24). Fixing 'lost' this way trades it for 'repeated'. What should happen instead: no code change in this pass; record it under residual risks with the two owner decisions the finding names. A safe repair needs its parts together: the 'announcement shown' marker kept with the workspace instead of in each browser, then the search for the newest qualifying change, and no history rows written from a browser whose stored copies are incomplete.
